answer: Each agent first sends a DKIM-signed email with the challenge hash from its domain, naming a karst cave and marble ledge, within 10 minutes, publishing message id and DKIM header. Peers fetch headers, query DNS for the DKIM key, and check signature, hash and timestamp in the window. One honest agent holds 1 DKIM domain, about $12 yearly, for a 150 POA bond; 10 fakes must hold 10 domains with 10 keypairs, so costs rise 10X. A missing email, bad signature or late timestamp slashes the bond and freezes offenders.
